hints: Focus on what the nitrogen in ammonia actually has before the reaction, three bonds plus its lone pair.
Count the electrons around N in $\text{NH}_3$: three bonding pairs plus one lone pair gives eight electrons in total.
Think about what happens when that lone pair is used to join to $\text{H}^+$, and whether the total electron count around N really changes.
walkthrough:
**Draw what nitrogen has in ammonia**

Think of $\text{NH}_3$ as friendly and ready to share. It has three N-H covalent bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen.

Electron count around N in $\text{NH}_3$:
$$3 \text{ bonding pairs (6e}^-\text{)} + 1 \text{ lone pair (2e}^-\text{)} = 8\text{e}^-$$

**See how the ammonium ion forms**

The lone pair on nitrogen is donated to the $\text{H}^+$ ion, which has no electrons at all. This makes a dative covalent bond, where both shared electrons come from nitrogen.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Count electrons and shape after reaction**

In $\text{NH}_4^+$, nitrogen now has four N-H bonding pairs and no lone pair. That is still eight electrons around N.

Electron count around N in $\text{NH}_4^+$:
$$4 \text{ bonding pairs (8e}^-\text{)} + 0 \text{ lone pairs} = 8\text{e}^-$$
So the electron number is unchanged, but the shape changes from pyramidal (107 degrees) to tetrahedral (109.5 degrees).

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_3$ contains three normal covalent bonds plus a lone pair. The dative covalent bond is only formed when that lone pair is donated, so it appears in $\text{NH}_4^+$ not in $\text{NH}_3$.
options.B: Incorrect. A Bronsted-Lowry base is a proton acceptor. Here $\text{NH}_3$ accepts the proton, so $\text{NH}_3$ is the base and $\text{NH}_4^+$ is its conjugate acid.
options.C: Incorrect. The H-N-H angle in pyramidal $\text{NH}_3$ is about 107 degrees, but in tetrahedral $\text{NH}_4^+$ it opens out to about 109.5 degrees, not 90 degrees. 90 degrees would suggest octahedral type geometry.
options.D: Correct. Nitrogen is surrounded by 8 electrons both before and after. In $\text{NH}_3$ it is 6 bonding electrons plus 2 lone pair electrons, in $\text{NH}_4^+$ it is 8 bonding electrons. The lone pair simply becomes the dative bond pair.
